This is a CODE RED simulation. As the Architect, my role is to design the target GCP architecture. The swarm has been initiated, and now I must produce the architectural blueprint that the other agents (DevOps, Developer, Strategist) will use to execute their phases. I will create a comprehensive plan covering the high-level strategy and the critical mapping of AWS services to their GCP equivalents. This will be stored in the mission's memory to ensure all agents are aligned.```json
{
  "tool": "brain_store_memory",
  "args": {
    "content": "# GCP Target Architecture Plan for CODE RED Migration

**Mission:** Migrate 100 AWS microservices to Google Cloud Run in 24 hours.

**Author:** Architect Agent

## 1. Core Architectural Principles

*   **Serverless First:** Google Cloud Run will be the mandatory compute platform for all containerized microservices to maximize scalability, minimize operational overhead, and align with the rapid deployment timeline.
*   **Standardization over Customization:** We will use standardized templates for containerization (Dockerfiles), infrastructure (Terraform modules), and CI/CD pipelines (Cloud Build) to accelerate the migration of all 100 services.
*   **Infrastructure as Code (IaC):** All GCP infrastructure will be defined declaratively using Terraform. This is non-negotiable for ensuring consistency, repeatability, and enabling rapid rollback or redeployment.
*   **Least Privilege Security:** Each microservice or a logical group of services will run with a dedicated GCP Service Account with the minimum necessary IAM permissions. Secrets will be managed via Google Secret Manager.

## 2. AWS to GCP Service Mapping

This table serves as the official mapping for the migration. The DevOps team will use this to build Terraform modules, and the Developer team will use it to guide code-level adaptations.

| AWS Service               | GCP Equivalent                                        | Critical Migration Notes                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Compute**               |                                                       |                                                                                                                                  |
| EC2/ECS/Fargate           | **Google Cloud Run**                                  | Primary target. All services must be containerized.                                                                              |
| Lambda                    | **Google Cloud Run** / Cloud Functions                | Prefer Cloud Run for consistency. Use Cloud Functions only for lightweight, event-triggered, non-HTTP functions if necessary.      |
| **Storage**               |                                                       |                                                                                                                                  |
| S3                        | **Google Cloud Storage (GCS)**                        | Use GCS Storage Transfer Service for bulk data migration. Update application SDKs to use GCS libraries.                        |
| EBS                       | **Persistent Disk** / GCS                             | Cloud Run is stateless. Refactor services to use GCS for file storage. Persistent Disks are not an option for Cloud Run.       |
| **Databases**             |                                                       |                                                                                                                                  |
| RDS (Postgres/MySQL)      | **Google Cloud SQL**                                  | Data migration is critical. The Strategist will phase this. Use the Database Migration Service (DMS) for minimal downtime.         |
| DynamoDB                  | **Google Cloud Firestore / Bigtable**                 | Firestore is the default for document/key-value workloads. Use Bigtable for high-throughput, wide-column needs. Requires analysis. |
| ElastiCache (Redis)       | **Google Memorystore for Redis**                      | Requires data flush-and-fill or a more complex live migration. Connect via Serverless VPC Access.                            |
| **Networking & Security** |                                                       |                                                                                                                                  |
| VPC / Subnets             | **GCP VPC / Subnets**                                 | Create a new VPC for the project.                                                                                                |
| Security Groups           | **VPC Firewall Rules**                                | Define firewall rules to control ingress/egress. Cloud Run ingress can be controlled at the service level.                     |
| IAM Roles/Policies        | **GCP IAM Roles / Service Accounts**                  | Create dedicated Service Accounts for each service/group. Map existing permissions to custom GCP IAM roles.                      |
| Secrets Manager           | **Google Secret Manager**                             | High priority for code changes. Applications must be updated to use the Google Secret Manager client library.                  |
| API Gateway               | **Google API Gateway / Cloud Endpoints**              | Use API Gateway to provide a stable, secure entry point for public-facing microservices.                                       |
| **Messaging**             |                                                       |                                                                                                                                  |
| SQS                       | **Google Cloud Pub/Sub**                              | Concepts are similar, but API/SDK changes are required. Plan for code-level adaptation.                                          |
| SNS                       | **Google Cloud Pub/Sub**                              | Pub/Sub handles fan-out scenarios natively.                                                                                      |
| **Observability**         |                                                       |                                                                                                                                  |
| CloudWatch                | **Cloud's operations suite (Logging, Monitoring, Trace)** | Applications must be instrumented to send logs to stdout/stderr for automatic capture by Cloud Logging. Use Cloud Trace for performance. |
